words.gloss_range: coordinating and resumptive opening particle attached to the following speech report

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: attached conjunction plus speech verb opening the reported denial

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) keeps 17:49 tied to the failed wayfinding just described in 17:48, so the quoted denial is heard as evidence of that diagnosis rather than as a detached objection. Because the particle is written into {{ar:وَقَالُوا}} ({{tr:wa-qālū}}), the transition into reported speech is compact: the reader moves at once from the prior assessment to the speakers' own proof against themselves.

topics.headline: the opening connector turns the quote into proof of the prior diagnosis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 17:49 displays the lostness named in 17:48 through the deniers' own speech.
topics.reason: The particle coherently links the ayah to 17:48 and opens the reported speech frame.

topics.headline: the proclitic form binds the connector to the speech verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the report begin without a hard pause between connection and speech.
topics.reason: The written and recited opening supports an immediate reported-speech launch.

words.gloss_range: they said; reported collective speech introducing direct quotation
words.root_gloss_range: saying, utterance, and voiced position; local form is a Form I perfect speech report

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: commanded reply form from the same speech root, cited as the answering counter-speech at 17:51

words.prose: {{ar:قَالُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:qālū}}) does not summarize the denial indirectly; it opens a direct quote whose whole remaining clause belongs to the speakers. The perfect plural form makes the denial a recorded collective utterance, while the shift from third-person report to first-person forms inside the quote lets the same group testify against itself; the long plural sonority then carries through the later we-forms. The speech verb also starts a familiar resurrection-denial template, answered by {{ar:قُل}} ({{tr:qul}}) at 17:51 and reprised with the same denial formula at 17:98.

topics.headline: the speech verb exposes the objection as direct quotation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the emphatic resurrection question is the deniers' own wording, not a narrator's paraphrase.
topics.reason: The following words are syntactically governed as quoted speech.

topics.headline: third-person report turns into first-person self-incrimination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks one group across the outside report and the inside quoted we.
topics.reason: The plural suffix and later first-person plural forms make the quoted voice continuous with the reported group.

topics.headline: the perfect Form I speech verb records a public position
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees disbelief externalized as a stated position rather than inferred as a private doubt.
topics.reason: The basic perfect speech form is locally coherent as a recorded act of saying.

topics.headline: the speech opener belongs to a repeated resurrection-denial formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes this quote as part of a recurring voiced-skepticism pattern, including 17:98, 13:5, and 23:82.
topics.reason: The inter-ayah rows give concrete formula parallels and same-surah reprise.

topics.headline: their saying prepares the commanded reply
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the quoted denial create the need for the command-speech response at 17:51.
topics.reason: The row family links the current reported speech to the nearby commanded answer.

words.gloss_range: interrogative hamza joined to a temporal condition particle

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: second interrogative opening the apodosis to the suspended condition

words.prose: {{ar:أَءِذَا}} ({{tr:a-idhā}}) opens the quoted objection by turning a temporal condition into an incredulous setup: when they have become bones and fragments, then what? The condition waits for {{ar:أَءِنَّا}} ({{tr:a-innā}}), so the ayah's denial is built as protasis and apodosis rather than as a single loose question. Variant handling narrows the point: readings that ease or omit the second hamza show where the audible pressure sits, but the local canonical form still carries overt question force.

topics.headline: the first question launches a suspended condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the objection unfold as an if-then challenge, with the resurrection clause still pending.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence explicitly links the protasis to the later apodosis.

topics.headline: the speakers treat decay as expected while disputing resurrection
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the split: decomposition is granted as the premise, while resurrection is made the target of denial.
topics.reason: The temporal condition and interrogative force coexist in the local particle cluster.

topics.headline: variant readings mark the sound-pressure without replacing the local parse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the question force is a precise form feature rather than a general mood supplied by the topic.
topics.reason: Accepted variants can illuminate hamza pressure, while the canonical local surface remains the governing form.

words.gloss_range: we were or will have become, in a copular conditional frame
words.root_gloss_range: being, becoming, and state; local Form I copula governs predicate states

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: temporal condition particle governing the future-completed viewpoint

words.prose: {{ar:كُنَّا}} ({{tr:kunnā}}) makes the speakers imagine themselves as having become the two material predicates that follow. The perfect form under {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}) views decomposition as a completed future state, while the first-person plural suffix turns the previously reported group into the quote's own we. The form is not causative; it names their state of becoming, and that state-claim is later answered by the command-and-creation logic of 17:51 and reprised in 17:98.

topics.headline: the verb makes bones and fragments predicate states
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speakers do not merely possess remains; they identify themselves with a reduced state.
topics.reason: The following accusative nouns are licensed as predicates of the copula.

topics.headline: perfect form under the condition presents decay as complete
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the deniers speak from an imagined future after decay has already happened.
topics.reason: The perfect copula is governed inside the temporal condition.

topics.headline: the suffix routes the outside group into quoted self-reference
topics.reader_payoff: The reader follows the same speakers from reported third person into their own first-person plural condition.
topics.reason: The bound pronoun supplies the subject of the copular state.

topics.headline: the being-root supplies state transition, not an external maker in this word
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the local form focus on becoming a state, while later creation language supplies the answer's agency.
topics.reason: The valid root range is narrowed by the local Form I copular grammar.

topics.headline: the state verb belongs to a denial formula answered nearby
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the imagined state of decay become a formulaic claim that 17:51 answers and 17:98 repeats.
topics.reason: The row family gives concrete same-surah and cross-surah formula references.

words.gloss_range: bones as an indefinite accusative predicate state
words.root_gloss_range: bigness, greatness, and bone/structural frame; local noun selects concrete bones

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: copular verb making the material nouns predicate states
coordinated second material predicate, crushed fragments or debris

words.prose: {{ar:عِظَٰمًۭا}} ({{tr:ʿiẓāman}}) is the first material predicate after {{ar:كُنَّا}} ({{tr:kunnā}}): the speakers imagine themselves as bones, not as owners of bones. Its indefinite broken plural makes the remaining framework multiple and exposed, with the emphatic sound giving the bone word a hard texture; then the following {{ar:رُفَٰتًا}} ({{tr:rufātan}}) pushes that framework toward pulverized debris. The root's broader greatness field is narrowed here to the concrete skeletal noun, but the load-bearing image still matters because the denial turns the bone stage of formation (23:14) into alleged evidence against re-creation; the same wording returns at 17:98 and appears in resurrection objections such as 23:82.

topics.headline: bones are a predicate state, not an object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speakers reduce their own future identity to a material state.
topics.reason: The word is syntactically the predicate of the copular verb.

topics.headline: matching accusatives bind bones to fragments
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the first material image prepared for escalation into the second.
topics.reason: The two nouns are parallel predicate states joined by the middle connector.

topics.headline: the broad root range narrows to concrete skeletal structure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps the load-bearing skeletal image without importing the full greatness field into the local sense.
topics.reason: The local noun is concrete bones, while the root-family association adds image pressure only within that limit.

topics.headline: the broken plural presents the frame as multiple remains
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a countable scatter of skeletal pieces before the mass debris noun arrives.
topics.reason: The form is a concrete broken plural and contrasts with the next mass-like noun.

topics.headline: bones shift from creation stage to denial proof
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a sign of formed embodiment is turned by the speakers into evidence against return.
topics.reason: The intertextual rows give creation-stage and resurrection-objection links.

topics.headline: the bone word returns in same-surah and cross-surah denial formulas
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the bone image as part of repeated resurrection skepticism, including 17:98.
topics.reason: Concrete echo rows support the formulaic role.

topics.headline: the emphatic sound gives the bone image hardness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the material hardness of the first decomposition term before the crumbling term softens it.
topics.reason: The phonetic observation reinforces the concrete image without changing the lexical sense.

words.gloss_range: coordinating particle between parallel accusative predicate states

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: second coordinated material predicate, crushed fragments or debris

words.prose: The middle {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) makes {{ar:رُفَٰتًا}} ({{tr:rufātan}}) a coordinated second predicate alongside {{ar:عِظَٰمًۭا}} ({{tr:ʿiẓāman}}). It does not make the second noun causal or merely appositional; it keeps the two material states equal enough to form one decomposition pair while still allowing the second term to intensify the first. The shared accusative cadence across the pair helps the physical descent sound unified.

topics.headline: the connector keeps both material states in parallel
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees bones and fragments as coordinated predicate states rather than one term swallowed by the other.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence licenses the second noun as conjoined with the first.

topics.headline: coordination allows a paired reading without erasing the two nouns
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear one decomposition complex while still tracking two distinct material images.
topics.reason: The hendiadys pressure is useful, but grammar still marks two coordinated predicate nouns.

topics.headline: the connector helps carry the shared cadence across the pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the two decomposition terms as one balanced acoustic unit.
topics.reason: The sound observation reinforces the grammatical pair.

words.gloss_range: crushed fragments, crumbled debris, pulverized remains as a coordinated predicate state
words.root_gloss_range: breaking, crushing, crumbling into fragments; local noun selects the result-state of disintegration
words.prose: {{ar:رُفَٰتًا}} ({{tr:rufātan}}) completes the speakers' self-description by moving from countable bones to a mass-like debris state. Its root pressure is not ordinary dust but crushing and disintegration, and its fricative and open-vowel texture lets the crumbling image spread in sound as the word closes the condition at maximum material breakdown. The rarity matters locally: the term appears in this same formulaic field and returns at 17:98, making this crumbling word a marked anchor of the resurrection objection rather than a generic synonym.

topics.headline: the second noun completes the self-description
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the fragments term governed by the same copular frame as bones.
topics.reason: The word is a coordinated accusative predicate in the conditional protasis.

topics.headline: the word carries pulverized result, not mere dust
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the objection intensify from skeletal remains to crushed debris.
topics.reason: The local noun preserves the root's crushing and crumbling result-image.

topics.headline: the result noun contrasts with the countable bone plural
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the material image shift from separate pieces to an undifferentiated debris state.
topics.reason: The form compresses the action of crumbling into a noun for the resulting state.

topics.headline: the rare crumbling term anchors the repeated formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the word as a marked formula term that returns in 17:98.
topics.reason: The profile and CRITICAL rows support rarity and same-surah formulaic recurrence.

topics.headline: the fragments term closes the condition at maximal decay
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the conditional setup stop at the strongest material premise the speakers can imagine.
topics.reason: The word is the final lexical item in the protasis before the apodosis begins.

topics.headline: the sound texture supports the crumbling image
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a softer spreading texture as the image moves from bone to debris.
topics.reason: The phonetic row reinforces the lexical image without controlling the parse.

words.gloss_range: interrogative hamza joined to emphatic particle with first-person plural subject
words.prose: {{ar:أَءِنَّا}} ({{tr:a-innā}}) supplies the apodosis to the suspended condition: after imagining themselves as bones and fragments, the speakers now question their own being raised. The form fuses question force with the emphatic particle and a definite first-person plural subject, so assertion-pressure and denial occupy the same word. Variant rows are useful only as form-pressure evidence: easing or omitting the hamza changes how explicit the question sounds, while the local canonical form remains an incredulous emphatic question that calls for the commanded answer at 17:51.

topics.headline: question force is fused to emphatic self-reference
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the speakers make their own resurrection the emphatic target of disbelief.
topics.reason: The particle governs the first-person suffix and introduces the questioned resurrection predicate.

topics.headline: the second interrogative answers the earlier condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah's architecture turn from the decay condition to the resurrection consequence.
topics.reason: The second question begins the apodosis linked to the earlier temporal condition.

topics.headline: variant readings expose hamza pressure without replacing the local form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the overt denial depends on the interrogative marker, even when variants show softer delivery.
topics.reason: The variant evidence is retained as contrast for question force, not as the governing local parse.

topics.headline: the quoted question creates the need for reply
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears why the reply in 17:51 must come as a directed answer to this quoted challenge.
topics.reason: The quote's second interrogative forms the challenge answered by the nearby command.

words.gloss_range: emphatic prefix attached to the resurrection predicate

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: emphatic first-person question whose predicate receives the lām
passive resurrection predicate emphasized by the lām

words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la-}}) binds emphasis directly to the passive resurrection predicate. Inside an incredulous question, that emphasis is not a calm affirmation; it is part of the speakers' heightened challenge, moving from the subject in {{ar:أَءِنَّا}} ({{tr:a-innā}}) to the predicate {{ar:مَبْعُوثُونَ}} ({{tr:mabʿūthūna}}). Its attachment lengthens the onset of the predicate and makes the denied claim sound weightier.

topics.headline: the prefix puts emphatic pressure on the resurrection predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the denial question sharpen around the predicate itself: are we indeed to be raised?
topics.reason: The particle scopes over the predicate of the emphatic clause.

topics.headline: the bound prefix fuses emphasis to the participle
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees and hears that emphasis enters as part of the predicate word's onset.
topics.reason: The lām is attached to the passive participle in the local surface.

words.gloss_range: raised or sent forth, locally passive participle for those raised in resurrection
words.root_gloss_range: raising, sending, dispatching, stirring into motion; local predicate selects passive resurrection raisedness

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: accusative creation phrase specifying the raised state

words.prose: {{ar:مَبْعُوثُونَ}} ({{tr:mabʿūthūna}}) is the predicate the emphatic question lands on: the speakers ask whether they will be made raised ones. The passive participle hides the raiser while foregrounding their patient status, and the sound masculine plural keeps the whole speaking group inside that raised status; the emphatic prefix and long plural ending give the predicate extra acoustic weight. The root's wider sending and stirring range remains relevant as motion-from-inertness pressure, but the local form and resurrection frame narrow it to being raised; the following {{ar:خَلْقًۭا}} ({{tr:khalqan}}) then specifies what kind of raisedness is being challenged. This passive resurrection wording belongs to a repeated denial field and returns at 17:98.

topics.headline: the passive participle is the raised-status predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause first establishes a passive raised status before adding the new-creation qualifier.
topics.reason: The word is syntactically the predicate of the emphatic particle.

topics.headline: the form suppresses the raiser and foregrounds the raised subjects
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the speakers' objection from the side of acted-upon humans while the agent remains grammatically unspoken.
topics.reason: The passive participle encodes patient status and does not name an active raiser.

topics.headline: plural participial form makes raisedness a collective status
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the whole speaking group carried into the predicate as a resulting status.
topics.reason: Agreement and participial form support collective status rather than a finite action alone.

topics.headline: sending and stirring pressure narrows to resurrection raising
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps the motion-from-inertness force of the root while reading the local predicate as resurrection raising.
topics.reason: The broader root range is valid, but local passive predicate and new-creation complement select resurrection.

topics.headline: the raised predicate is completed by the new-creation tail
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the question become not merely whether they are raised, but raised into a new created state.
topics.reason: The following accusative phrase is attached as a state or specification of the predicate.

topics.headline: the passive resurrection predicate belongs to a repeated denial field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes this predicate as part of a wider resurrection objection pattern, including 17:98 and 11:7.
topics.reason: The row family supplies concrete parallel references for the passive predicate field.

topics.headline: the predicate carries acoustic weight
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the emphatic prefix and long plural ending give the resurrection predicate extra weight.
topics.reason: The surface form combines emphatic prefix, passive participle, and plural ending.

topics.headline: the denied way is specified as return by resurrection
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the prior lost path become concretely the path back from death that they deny.
topics.reason: The topic coherently links the predicate to the surrounding surah's way and raising field.

words.gloss_range: creation, created state, or act/process of creating in an accusative qualifying role
words.root_gloss_range: creating, shaping, measured formation, and in some contexts fabrication; local phrase concerns renewed creation

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: accusative adjective agreeing with and qualifying the creation noun

words.prose: {{ar:خَلْقًۭا}} ({{tr:khalqan}}) turns the predicate into a question about mode and identity: being raised as, or in respect of, a new creation. Its accusative form can be read as state or specification, and the maṣdar keeps act and product close together rather than counting separate creatures. The word also controls {{ar:جَدِيدًۭا}} ({{tr:jadīdan}}), so newness belongs to the creation phrase specifically. The root field gives the deniers' wording a double edge: they treat renewed formation as impossible, yet the phrase belongs to a stable Quranic new-creation formula that is answered in 17:51, reprised in 17:98, and echoed in passages such as 14:19 and 13:5.

topics.headline: the accusative tail can specify state, kind, or act
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final phrase expand the resurrection question beyond the bare fact of being raised.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence allows state or specification readings.

topics.headline: the singular verbal noun keeps process and product together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final noun names a mode of renewed making, not multiple counted creations.
topics.reason: The form is an indefinite singular maṣdar in an accusative qualifying role.

topics.headline: the creation noun governs the final adjective
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees newness attached to the creation phrase rather than floating as a loose adverbial idea.
topics.reason: The following adjective agrees with this noun in case and indefiniteness.

topics.headline: creation and fabrication senses sharpen the deniers' wording
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the speakers use a word that can name real formation even while they frame resurrection as implausible.
topics.reason: The broader root range is retained as quoted-word pressure, while local syntax keeps renewed creation as the selected phrase sense.

topics.headline: the word holds renewed making and created state together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees resurrection challenged as both an act of renewed making and the resulting created state.
topics.reason: The gerund and accusative role allow act and product readings to remain jointly visible.

topics.headline: the phrase belongs to a stable formula answered nearby
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes that the deniers' final phrase prepares the origin-creation answer in 17:51 and the later reprise in 17:98.
topics.reason: The row family gives same-surah and cross-surah formula references, including 17:51 and 17:98.

topics.headline: the compact final tail qualifies the raised predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the clause land on the contested characterization, not stop at the passive predicate.
topics.reason: The final accusative phrase follows and qualifies the completed passive predicate.

topics.headline: one row discusses the wrong aligned root
topics.blocking_evidence: QAC aligns word 11 with {{ar:خَلْقًۭا}} ({{tr:khalqan}}) from {{ar:خ ل ق}} ({{tr:kh-l-q}}), while the row discusses domains of {{ar:ب ع ث}} ({{tr:b-ʿ-th}}).
topics.reason: The claim may be valid for word 10 but is unsuitable as a topic for the aligned word 11.

words.gloss_range: new, fresh, renewed as an accusative indefinite adjective modifying the creation noun
words.root_gloss_range: newness, freshness, renewal, and in wider family seriousness or striving; local adjective selects new or renewed quality

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: creation noun modified by the final adjective

words.prose: {{ar:جَدِيدًۭا}} ({{tr:jadīdan}}) is the final adjective and the ayah's last sound, locking newness onto {{ar:خَلْقًۭا}} ({{tr:khalqan}}) by case and indefiniteness. Its range allows both new and renewed/restored resonance, so the speakers' phrase cannot force a choice between replacement and restoration. After bones and crushed fragments, this closing adjective reverses the material descent with the possibility they reject, while the shared accusative tanwīn thread links the material nouns to the renewal phrase. It also belongs to the stable new-creation formula found in passages such as 14:19, 13:5, 32:10, 34:7, 35:16, and 50:15, returns at 17:98, and anticipates the first-origination answer in 17:51.

topics.headline: the final adjective is locked to the creation noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees newness qualify the creation phrase specifically, not the raising predicate in isolation.
topics.reason: The adjective agrees with the preceding noun in case and indefiniteness.

topics.headline: the adjective turns decay toward fresh renewal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the final word contest the deniers' decay premise from inside their own wording.
topics.reason: The semantic range of new and renewed fits the local resurrection question.

topics.headline: wider root-family pressure narrows to adjective newness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps renewal and restoration pressure while reading the local word as an adjective of the creation phrase.
topics.reason: The root-family associations are useful only insofar as they inform the selected qualitative adjective.

topics.headline: the closing tanwīn makes newness the recited endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah land not on fragments but on the denied possibility of renewal.
topics.reason: The adjective is the final word and carries the ayah-ending cadence.

topics.headline: matching accusative cadence links decay terms to renewal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the material nouns and the final renewal phrase bound by a shared ending pattern.
topics.reason: The shared accusative indefiniteness and cadence are locally visible across the sequence.

topics.headline: the adjective belongs to a stable new-creation formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the deniers' closing word as part of a Quranic formula for divine creative power, not a one-off insult.
topics.reason: The adjective strongly collocates with the creation noun in new-creation contexts.

topics.headline: the closing adjective seals repeated quoted objections
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the same closing word function as the seal of denial in 17:98 and related quoted objections such as 32:10 and 34:7.
topics.reason: The rows give concrete reported-speech parallels and same-surah reprise.

topics.headline: the final word frames the whole movement toward the answer

topics.reason: The local sequence and nearby answer make the final adjective an arc marker.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The progression from bones to crumbled remains and then to the passive prospect of being raised.
baseline_models.mechanism: The speakers move the body from its last recognizable hard frame into dispersed debris, then treat that loss of organization as the limiting case for renewed motion and agency.

activation_trace.role: The hard skeletal member supplies the body's last coherent structural frame.
Breaking into scattered debris supplies the irreversible-looking loss of bodily organization.
Stirring what lies still supplies the minimal return of motion tested by the passive resurrection term.

changed_reading.before: The verse asks generally whether life follows death.
changed_reading.after: The verse tests whether agency can re-enter matter after the body has crossed from solid frame to dispersed fragments.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The predication of a new creation after the stated reduction to fragmented remains.
baseline_models.mechanism: Creation as prior proportioning combines with newness that occurs across a severance: the questioned act is not merely replacement, but a newly measured embodiment on the far side of material discontinuity.

activation_trace.role: Prior measuring and proportioning make renewed embodiment intelligible as specified form rather than accidental aggregation.
Novel occurrence after a break lets the adjective retain the discontinuity instead of erasing it.
A cord severed into pieces supplies the break across which the renewed form must preserve continuity.

changed_reading.before: A new creation sounds like an unrelated replacement for the former body.
changed_reading.after: It can denote a re-proportioned embodiment whose novelty occurs across, and therefore answers, the body's severance.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The quoted double interrogative: first a hypothetical state of decay, then an emphatic question about the speakers themselves.
baseline_models.mechanism: The first question installs decomposition as a premise and the second voices its alleged consequence; the utterance therefore performs a committed supposition more than an open request for information.

activation_trace.role: Saying that functions as supposition, especially under interrogation, makes the quotation an inferential stance.
Coming to be in time turns bodily decay into the premise on which the skeptical conclusion is made to rest.

changed_reading.before: The speakers neutrally ask what will happen after decay.
changed_reading.after: They package decay as a premise that is meant already to decide the answer, so the question acts as denial.

context_deltas.mechanism: Varied presentation is followed not by recollection but by amplified withdrawal, making the focus utterance one possible output of a response loop in which further articulation hardens the skeptical stance.

activation_trace.role: The interrogative supposition anchors the response loop in the focus speakers' voiced inference.
Turning something through different states supplies repeated reformulation rather than a single exposure.
Increase and growth supply the counterintuitive amplification of resistance.
Recoiling away supplies the direction into which that amplified response moves.

structural_cues: 17:41 places varied recitation, intended recollection, increase, and recoil before the argumentative sequence that reaches the focus.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: 17:41 supplies a reformulation-to-recoil sequence. Reader: repeated presentation feeds the stance voiced in 17:49. Alternative: the recoil may characterize the wider audience without causing this exact utterance.

changed_reading.before: The denial is a one-time judgment about decayed matter.
changed_reading.after: It can be heard as a hardened response produced by repeated encounters that increase distance rather than understanding.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context layers failure to grasp, an intervening veil, protective coverings, auditory weight, and listening without receptive compliance; the focus's material premise is thereby relocated from objective proof to a constrained mode of reception.

activation_trace.role: The interrogative supposition anchors the epistemic constraint in the focus utterance itself.
Failure of grasping supplies the first explicit limit on what the speakers can infer from the world.
A screening barrier supplies separation between recitation and receptive access.
A preserving cover becomes functionally an enclosure that keeps the heart from receiving the claim.
Auditory heaviness supplies a bodily image for hearing that does not become comprehension.
Hearing whose full branch includes understanding and compliance exposes the gap between acoustic attendance and receptive response.

structural_cues: 17:44-47 repeatedly contrast pervasive signs or recitation with non-understanding, screening, weighted hearing, and hostile listening.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: the sequence supplies layered reception failures. Reader: those failures condition the premise asserted in 17:49, so material decay is being read through an occluded channel. Alternative: the barriers may mark moral refusal independently of the resurrection argument.

changed_reading.before: Decay is presented as publicly available evidence against resurrection.
changed_reading.after: The same premise becomes evidence of the speakers' restricted reception: they hear the claim while the route from sign to understanding remains blocked.

context_deltas.mechanism: Immediately before the focus, the speakers are described as manufacturing comparisons that leave them unable to find a path. Their bones-and-fragments scenario can therefore be read as one such analogy: a present material state is made to dictate the limit of future divine action.

activation_trace.role: The uttered supposition anchors the manufactured comparison in the focus question.
Fragmented debris provides the selected image from which the speakers extrapolate impossibility.
Actively depicting a comparison supplies the operation by which the corpse image is made argumentative.
A deliberately set comparison supplies the inferential vehicle rather than a neutral observation.
Deviation from the intended direction marks the comparison's reasoning effect.
A traversable route supplies what the manufactured analogy prevents them from finding.

structural_cues: 17:48 ends with failed comparisons and no path; 17:49 begins with a quoted material comparison.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: 17:48 supplies comparison-making and resulting pathlessness immediately before the focus. Reader: the bones-and-fragments premise is one of those comparisons. Alternative: 17:48 may refer only to the preceding characterization of the messenger.

changed_reading.before: Fragmentation straightforwardly demonstrates why resurrection is implausible.
changed_reading.after: Fragmentation is a selected analogy that becomes a trap: it projects the limits of a broken object onto the agency that would recreate it.

context_deltas.mechanism: The reply does not retreat from the speakers' material test; it drives it in the opposite direction, from dispersed fragments to stone and resistant iron. If even maximally hard matter remains within scope, no position on the fragmented-to-solid scale controls the possibility of being raised.

activation_trace.role: Dispersed breakage supplies the speakers' chosen material extreme.
Stirring inert matter anchors the reply's material reversal in the questioned act.
Hard stone supplies a compact material state opposite to scattered remains.
Resistant metallic solidity intensifies the counterexample beyond ordinary bodily matter.

structural_cues: 17:50 is the immediate imperative answer and substitutes denser materials for the focus's decomposed materials.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: the reply supplies stone and iron after bones and fragments. Reader: the sequence reverses the speakers' scale of material impossibility. Alternative: the imperative may function as hyperbole without proposing a systematic material scale.

changed_reading.before: Resurrection becomes less plausible as the body's matter loses cohesion.
changed_reading.after: Cohesion and hardness are equally irrelevant: the reply ranges across material states to deny that matter sets the limit.

context_deltas.mechanism: The reply repeats creation, names return, and points to the first origination. This binds the focus's newness to continuity of origin: the later embodiment is a new event, but its subject is returned through the same originating agency rather than replaced by an unrelated product.

activation_trace.role: Measured specification anchors identity in an ordered form that can be enacted again.
New occurrence after discontinuity supplies the apparent tension with personal return.
The repeated creation noun keeps the reply on the focus anchor while widening the range of possible material.
Return after departure supplies persistence of the same addressees across the break.
Origination and beginning identify the agency that can repeat the act without losing its subject.
Priority and firstness make the initial embodiment the explicit precedent for the later one.

structural_cues: 17:51 answers who will restore the speakers by pointing to their first origination.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: 17:51 supplies repeated creation, return, origination, and firstness. Reader: these terms preserve personal continuity inside the focus's newness. Alternative: new may emphasize only a fresh event, leaving the mode of numerical identity unstated.

changed_reading.before: New creation threatens to mean replacement of the old persons by new copies.
changed_reading.after: Newness names the renewed event and form, while return to the first originating act keeps the same addressees in view.

context_deltas.mechanism: The questioned raising unfolds next as summons and response, then as regulation of what servants say. Resurrection thus restores not only organized matter but directed, answer-capable speech; the present skeptical utterance anticipates a future condition of answerability.

activation_trace.role: Dispatching a sent agent lets being raised include restored directed agency rather than motion alone.
Voiced speech anchors answerability in the speakers' present act.
A directed summons supplies the initiating relation into which the raised persons re-enter.
Returning an answer supplies the restored human capacity elicited by the summons.
The renewed command about speaking links present utterance to accountable verbal agency.
The good as the opposite of the ugly supplies the evaluative standard governing that restored speech.

structural_cues: 17:52 renders the event as call and response; 17:53 immediately returns to commanded human speech.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: the post-focus sequence supplies summons, response, and a norm for saying. Reader: raised agency is therefore dialogical and answerable, and 17:49's saying already belongs to that arc. Alternative: 17:53 may begin a separate ethical instruction rather than specify resurrection.

changed_reading.before: Being raised means that a body is reconstructed and made animate.
changed_reading.after: Being raised restores a person as one who can be summoned, answer, praise, and bear responsibility for speech.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The activation is surprising because one root moves from evaluative magnitude in 17:40 to literal skeleton in 17:49. It remains valid as an exact root-and-branch echo attached to the focus noun and to an earlier evaluation of the speakers' saying. Downstream prose should present it as a rhetorical resonance, not claim that the two senses are lexically interchangeable.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus noun for bones shares its root with the earlier description of the speakers' saying as immense.

activation_trace.role: The skeletal sense supplies the concrete material on which the skeptical argument is built.
Magnitude and force supply an evaluative echo that makes the later bone-argument itself sound overgrown.
Overtly emitted speech ties the earlier evaluation to the focus's renewed quotation.

changed_reading.before: Bones are only the physical evidence named by the speakers.
changed_reading.after: Through the root echo, the bones also carry a secondary judgment on the scale of the saying built from them.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is a form-distant activation from the packet's alternate mapped target for the focus speech root, not an ordinary gloss of the verb. It remains anchored because the packet explicitly resolves that target from focus word 1 and its motion image coheres with a question that destabilizes continuity. Downstream prose should label it a sonic-material analogy and never substitute it for the normal speech sense.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The opening speech verb, read through its non-dominant mapped inventory alongside the question's unstable body-state.

activation_trace.role: Rattling motion and lack of fixedness turn the opening utterance into a verbal disturbance around bodily continuity.
Temporal coming-to-be supplies the changing state that the exploratory verbal disturbance circles.

changed_reading.before: The opening speech merely reports a fixed skeptical proposition.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the utterance itself rattles around the feared instability of becoming fragments and being made anew.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The body-to-settlement transfer is cross-domain and therefore surprising, but it remains anchored in the focus's sequence of organized structure, destruction, and rising, while 17:58 supplies an assembled settlement destined for destruction before the rising. Downstream prose should frame this only as a scale analogy, not identify a town with a body.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The body's organized frame becomes debris before being raised.

activation_trace.role: Fragmentation supplies the destruction stage in the focus's individual-scale sequence.
Reactivation of what lies still anchors the final stage back in the focus.
A settlement as gathered people supplies an organized collective body at a larger scale.
Falling into destruction supplies the collective analogue to bodily disintegration.
The branch's rising and resurrection sense places collective destruction before the same terminal horizon.

changed_reading.before: The question concerns only whether one ruined organism can return.
changed_reading.after: As a contained scale analogy, it participates in a wider pattern in which organized human structures, bodily or civic, pass through destruction before rising.

strongest_changes: 17:48 makes the bones-and-fragments premise legible as a manufactured comparison that produces its own pathlessness.
17:50-51 reverses the material test and binds new creation to return and first origination.
17:52-53 turns being raised from reassembly alone into restored answerability and accountable speech.
summary.what_was_special: The immediate sequence moves from failed comparison, through harder matter and first origination, to summons and response; the focus is the hinge where a material objection is converted into a question of agency, continuity, and answerability.
remaining_uncertainties: The newness-after-severance reading is branch-grounded but may exceed what the adjective alone carries in ordinary usage.
The reception barriers strongly frame the discourse, but their causal relation to this exact utterance remains reader-supplied.
The magnitude-to-bones echo and alternate speech-root activation should remain explicitly exploratory.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **They mistake fragmentation for loss of measured form.** `ع ظ م:B005` is bone, `ر ف ت:B001` scattered fragments, `ب ع ث:B001` rouses stillness, `خ ل ق:B001/B002` measures and originates, and `ج د د:B003/B004` cuts then renews. The objection moves from hard structure to dispersed pieces, but creation's branch already includes proportioning before origination. I infer they equate material continuity with formal possibility. “New creation” reads as remeasuring after severance, directly answering that assumption.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:98 repeats this objection verbatim after the sensory reversal of 17:97. Its return revealed the material argument as a pattern that eventually shapes the objector's own body.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **The objection mistakes fragmentation for unrecoverable loss of form.** Lexical evidence: `ر ف ت B001` (breaking into scattered fragments) in `رُفَٰتًا`, `ب ع ث B001` (rousing a still thing into motion) in `مَبْعُوثُونَ`, `خ ل ق B001` (measuring and proportioning a thing) in `خَلْقًا`, and `ج د د B004` (newness after cutting) in `جَدِيدًا`. Structural cue: 17:48 diagnoses disabling representations; 17:50–51 deliberately extends the imagined material resistance, then invokes first origination, and 17:52 depicts one call reorganizing the sleepers into response. Assigned role: fragmentation disperses components, rousing restores motion, proportion restores form, and newness-after-cutting names reconstitution across discontinuity. Abductive move: the packet supplies first creation as precedent; I infer that the capacity to proportion initially also answers dispersed matter. Reading change: resurrection becomes a reorganization problem the Creator's prior act already models, exposing the objection's hidden equation of disassembly with impossibility.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:52 was the decisive later activation: immediate answering by the formerly dispersed made `ب ع ث B001` read as responsive reorganization, not only renewed material motion.

findings.text: Kemiklerin parçalanması biçimin ölçüsünün de kaybolduğu sanısına dayanır; oysa yeni yaratma, kopmuş malzemeyi yeniden ölçüp düzenleme imkânını içerir.

inter_ayah_rows.note: Repeats the objection verbatim and frames it as the cause of rejection, adding its consequence.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Adds the earth-to-earth-to-emergence sequence, directly answering dispersion with return.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Contrasts the first creation with khalq jadid and locates the obstacle in human confusion.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Parallels the objection with dust and bones, extending the material state named in 17:49.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Immediately broadens the resistant material challenge from fragments to stone and iron.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Adds that collective creation and ba'th are as one self, addressing scale rather than remains.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: A close parallel using death, dust, and bones; it confirms the recurring objection without adding a new answer.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Immediately identifies the originator of the first creation as the one who returns them.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Adds replacement by a new creation, a secondary sense of khalq jadid rather than bodily return.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Parallels the death-dust-bones objection and prepares its later response in the passage.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Supplies the summoned response and the altered sense of elapsed time after the question in 17:49.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses ba'atha for a person's rising to act, not return after bodily dissolution.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Pairs loss in the earth with khalq jadid and identifies refusal of the meeting with the Lord.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Material comparison and claimed superiority offer a contrary reduction of created form, not resurrection.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Mentions denial that God will ba'atha anyone, but the referent and material question differ.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Sharpens the objection by naming bones as decayed and hollowed.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Completes the immediate sequence with cosmic creation as evidence for recreating human like forms.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Poses the bones-in-decay challenge, but adds no answer within this ayah itself.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: States a general denial of ba'th without the material reasoning of 17:49.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Creation and final return occur in a different dispute about human status and authority.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Adds ba'th as the premise that exposes unjust practice, not its material possibility.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Restates the soil-to-khalq-jadid objection and explicitly treats it as disbelief.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Shows a contrary reduction of Adam to clay within the same nearby creation narrative.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Ba'atha here concerns sending a messenger, not resurrection.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Invokes human creation from clay as an argument from originating material.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Iron here belongs to punishment imagery, not the reconstitution challenge.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Directly answers the bone problem through their complete gathering.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: No creation, return, or resurrection connection is stated.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Shares the nearby Adam narrative and the Day of Resurrection, but not the question of re-creation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Parallels death, dust, and bones while adding accountability as the disputed outcome.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Concerns hearing and reason in punishment, with no return or creation link.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Re-entry into punishment is a contrary return loop, not bodily re-creation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Adds universal ba'th and disclosure of deeds, extending the stakes beyond material restoration.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Shows bones being formed, covered, and made another creation, supplying a formation sequence.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Adds creation followed by forming, relevant to form but outside the death-and-return question.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: States plainly that those in graves will be raised.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses the sky's construction as a scale comparison for creation, indirectly challenging impossibility.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Links the originator of heaven and earth with this world and the next, without reconstitution detail.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Repeats death, dust, bones, and emergence as the contested promise.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Parallels dust and ancestral remains, adding an emergence formulation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Adds the possibility of removal and a new creation, a secondary replacement reading.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Places ba'th beyond an intervening barrier, adding temporal sequence after death.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Questions return to a prior condition, preserving the objection in a compressed form.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Pairs giving life and death with cosmic alternation, supporting divine command over life.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Gives an instance of being raised after death, without the dispersed-remains issue.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Condenses the same death-to-dust objection as an allegedly distant return.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses the Day of Resurrection only as the limit of reprieve.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Directly questions emergence alive after death, though it omits the bone imagery.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Contrasts beings unable to create with beings themselves created, supporting the creator premise.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Names total fragmentation and khalq jadid in a mocking formulation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Generic creator-versus-noncreator contrast supplies only a broad capability premise.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Concerns false accusation and speech, with no relevant creation or return theme.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses judad for visible mountain bands; the lexical resemblance does not address new creation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Concerns a community's admission at punishment, not ba'th or re-creation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Notes individual creation, but adds no return, death, or formation argument.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Joins cosmic creation with explicit denial of being raised after death.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses the Day of Resurrection as a deadline for Iblis, not evidence about re-creation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Concerns a denial of association, not creation or resurrection.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses the fact of first creation to demand affirmation in the resurrection argument of its passage.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Distinguishes human participation from the act of creating, supporting the creator premise.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Counters denial of ba'th with an oath, certainty, and subsequent accounting.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Concerns informed recounting, with no stated resurrection connection.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Generic creation establishes origin but does not address dissolution or return.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Concerns access to prior scripture, not creation or resurrection.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Names the creator of earth and high heavens in a revelation setting only.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Concerns purification and inheritance in the garden, not re-creation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Adds that the time of ba'th is unknown, not whether dispersed bodies can return.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Explicitly addresses doubt in ba'th through human development and reviving earth.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Names the Day of Resurrection as a setting for a prayer, without material relevance.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Concerns closed hearts and disbelief, not the focus question.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Cosmic creation supports a broad creator premise but no return is stated.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Concerns questioning at death and migration, not resurrection.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Cosmic signs and alternation offer only a general creation analogy.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Adds successive creations in the womb, a formation analogy rather than post-death return.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Identifies the Day of Resurrection as the denied reality and corrects perceived duration.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Concerns divine sonship and universal submission, not re-creation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Shows death, raising, bones reassembled and covered, plus altered elapsed-time perception.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Concerns character, not creation or return.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses the Day of Resurrection as a temporal endpoint in a separate narrative.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Concerns religious affiliation, not creation or resurrection.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Invites reflection on an existing creature's creation, a remote origin analogy.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Concerns demands to alter revelation, not return after death.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Calls people to worship their creator and prior generations, without a re-creation claim.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Ba'atha here appoints Saul as king, not resurrection.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Directly states that people will be raised on the Day of Resurrection.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Concerns unsupported claims about the garden, not creation or return.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses prior creation from nothing as a strong antecedent for later re-creation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Concerns a claim about limited fire, not resurrection.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Names being raised alive as a life-stage threshold, without the material objection.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Names weakening bone, but in a prayer about old age rather than reconstitution.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Depicts universal appearance before God and judgment, only indirectly presupposing return.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Creator knowledge is a broad premise but does not address re-forming remains.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Concerns dispute in the fire, not resurrection or creation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Acknowledges cosmic creation but gives no step from it to human re-creation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Contrasts worldly provision with the hereafter, without resurrection wording or argument.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Explicitly sets beginning creation beside repeating it and declares that easy.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Concerns the Quran's majesty, not creation or return.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Human origin from a drop and ensuing dispute is only a remote origin contrast.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: No creation, return, or resurrection connection is stated.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Cosmic creation and governance provide a general authority premise only.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Sets death, life, death, renewed life, and return in a single sequence.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Presents a concrete restoration-from-death sign and directs attention to its force.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Gives a collective death-and-revival instance, expanding the question beyond one body.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Shows separated parts restored to life, closely engaging dispersal and reassembly.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Preserves a secondary life-from-death sign while explicitly locating it under divine permission.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Asserts unavoidable gathering on the Day of Resurrection.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Reiterates life-from-death as a sign under divine permission.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Directly answers that God will raise the dead despite human refusal to hear.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Pairs emergence of living from dead with its converse as a creation pattern.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses movement from death to life as an experiential analogy, not bodily reassembly.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Adds replacement and succession after originating a people, a secondary new-creation reading.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Sets life, death, and emergence from the earth together.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses revived dead land as an explicit analogy for bringing forth the dead.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Joins universal return with beginning and repeating creation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Challenges deniers through the question of who begins creation and repeats it.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Pairs giving life and death with return to God.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: States divine giving of life and death and enduring inheritance after creatures pass.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Records the denial of resurrection and answers it with a binding divine promise.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses rain-revived earth as a sign for life after its death.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Makes the Hour's promise central to the discovery scene, though no material mechanism is given.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Adds complete gathering with no one left behind after worldly forms are displaced.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Depicts return in ordered presentation before the Lord after initial creation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses prior creation from nothing as a direct rebuttal to doubting renewed existence.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Challenges any earthly source claimed able to raise the dead.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Pairs death with eventual return, adding the testing frame rather than reassembly.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Makes repetition of initial creation the stated pattern for a new creation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Combines divine truth and power with giving life to the dead.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Pairs life, death, and renewed life under the same divine agency.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Supplies the death stage immediately before the resurrection assertion already represented by 23:16.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Links human originating faculties with eventual gathering.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: States scattering and gathering as a paired divine operation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Marks the present objection as a recurrence of an earlier refusal without restating its material terms.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Adds the ancestral and repeated-promise dimension to the same denial sequence.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Links purposeful creation with return to God, challenging a no-return premise.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Names death followed by being given life in a direct first-person formulation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Pairs beginning creation, repeating it, and return from earth in one challenge.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Pairs every soul's death with return, supplying the universal transition.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses rain-revived earth as a direct sign of life after death.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: States beginning creation, repeating it, and return in sequence.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Pairs bringing living from dead with bringing dead from living and reviving earth.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Names repetition after initial creation and declares it more readily conceived.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Unites creation, provision, death, and life under one agent.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Explicitly compares reviving dead land with raising the dead.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses dead land made alive as the stated likeness for resurrection.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Directly states that the dead are given life and their traces are recorded.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses dead earth revived into provision as a sign.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Adds emergence from graves in response to the trumpet.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Voices the surprised question of who raised those from their resting place.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Sets human origin from a drop against the later disputation over creation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Answers the bone question by returning it to the first creator.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses a life-bearing transformation in green wood as a secondary material counterexample.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses creation of heavens and earth as an explicit capacity argument for recreating humans.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Adds the command formulation for bringing a matter into being.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Extends the resurrection objection by explicitly including forefathers.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Distinguishes the taking and releasing of souls, offering a secondary account of death's boundary.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Adds the trumpet sequence in which death is followed by standing and looking on.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Acknowledges two deaths and two lives, directly contesting final extinction.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses the greater creation of heavens and earth as an argument relevant to human re-creation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Pairs life and death with the bringing-to-be command.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Makes revived dead earth an explicit sign that the dead can be given life.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: States that the one who gives life to the dead has power over all things.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Names emergence after death through the analogy of revived land.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: States the no-return claim in the form of death as finality.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Pairs that finality claim with a demand concerning forefathers.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Records the claim that only worldly life, death, and time exist.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Shows the resurrection claim being met by the same ancestral challenge.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Pairs death, life, and gathering on the Day without doubt.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Restates the dust-and-emergence objection within a family dispute.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses creation of heavens and earth as an explicit proof of power to give life to the dead.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses water and dead land to prepare the emergence image.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Explicitly labels the emergence from revived land as the coming forth.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Adds the summons heard from a near place, complementing 17:52's call-and-response.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Names the day of emergence from graves.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Depicts people emerging from graves in a resurrection scene.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Introduces replacement by forms not known, a secondary bodily-renewal reading.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses knowledge of the first creation as the prompt to remember re-creation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Pairs giving life and death with comprehensive divine power.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Depicts rapid emergence from graves toward a set marker.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Adds exact restoration down to fingertips after the bone-gathering question.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses daily taking and raising as a recurrent, though non-bodily, return pattern.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Depicts individual arrival before God, presupposing return without describing resurrection.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Adds the trumpet and universal gathering in the final scene.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Universal mortality makes continued worldly life unavailable to the questioners.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Adds the trumpet as the point at which ordinary worldly relations cease.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Sets observation of first creation beside the later creation it entails.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Frames death as a taking after which people are returned to their Lord.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Counters denial of the Hour and anchors the claim in comprehensive knowledge.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Condenses the resurrection event into one cry followed by universal presentation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses reversal in lifespan as a secondary reflection on bodily condition, not resurrection itself.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Contrasts the first death with a later state in the passage's resurrection setting.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: States the Hour's certainty alongside widespread disbelief.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Shows the denied reality becoming manifest at judgment.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Explicitly pairs replacement of like forms with bringing forth in an unknown form.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses human emergence from earth as an origin image before the return-and-extraction sequence.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Pairs return to earth with a subsequent extraction from it.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Ends the human formation sequence by asking about power to give life to the dead.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Adds the trumpet as the event that brings people forth in groups.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Makes the transition depend on a single overwhelming cry.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Shows the formerly questioning people suddenly present on the open ground.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Names graves being overturned as a final-disclosure event.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Depicts the earth casting out what it contains, a direct emergence image.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Affirms power to return the human being, though it leaves the return's form unstated.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Uses the earth's expulsion of its burdens in the final upheaval.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P3 (17:40-60): Resistant Matter Reconstituted by a Summons
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Material disintegration and apparent hardness do not prevent a new formation when the originating power calls the dispersed subject back.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Resurrection is modeled as fresh measurement after cutting, while response functions like a piercing answer through apparently closed material.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Bone, Fragment, Stone, and Iron Remade
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Dispersed organic remains and resistant mineral bodies are all returned to a newly measured form by the originator.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: hard bone (`quranic:root_001029:B005/m01`); pulverized remains (`quranic:root_000578:B001/m01`); solid stone (`quranic:root_000296:B003/m01`); resistant iron (`quranic:root_000002:B004/m01`); measuring a form (`quranic:root_000434:B001/m01`); originating existence (`quranic:root_000434:B002/m01`); opening and splitting (`quranic:root_001165:B001/m01`); origination and beginning (`quranic:root_001165:B002/m01`); newness after cutting (`quranic:root_000227:B004/m01`); return after departure (`quranic:root_001058:B001/m01`); skeptical head-motion (`quranic:root_001526:B001/m01`)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The objection moves from decay to maximal resistance, but both are placed inside the same productive operation. Creation is measurement and origination; newness itself carries the trace of a prior cut. The head's skeptical oscillation becomes a small bodily rehearsal of the return it denies.

branches.source_phrase_ar: العرب تجري تقول وحدها في الاستفهام مجرى تظن في العمل (sihah)؛ بنو سليم يجرون متصرف قلت في غير الاستفهام أيضا مجرى الظن (sihah)

source_note.SI: Tekil aktarım, sanmak gibi işleyen söyleme kullanımını ve soru dışına uzanan lehçe notunu verir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi dışa vurulmadan önce zihinde tasarlanan veya kişinin içinde tuttuğu sözü anlatır. Geçici çerçeve bu iç söz anlamını doğru verir ve sesli söyleme ile inanç anlamlarını dışarıda bırakır.

source_note.MU: Tekil aktarım, işitilen hitap olmaksızın içe doğan anlamın söz diye adlandırılmasını verir.

root_profile.summary: Bu kök, sesle söze dökme çekirdeğinden konuşma organı, konuşkan kişi, eski unvan, yalan isnat, söylenti, müzakere, hüküm dayatma, iç söz, görüş benimseme, sözsüz belirtme, içten önemseme, teknik tanım ve içe doğan anlam gibi ayrı dallara yayılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi azlığı çokluğun karşıtı olarak verir; ayrıca yoksulluk, düşüklük, bir şeyi az görme ve belirli yapılarda yokluğa ya da seyrekliğe yaklaşan kullanımları açıkça destekler.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol yalnızca sayı ve miktar azlığını ve buna bağlı kullanımları kapsar; yükseklik, kap, taşıma ve titreme anlamlarını kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Temel azlık anlamı ile yoksullaşma ve az görme gibi türemiş biçimler birlikte bulunur; yokluk ve seyrekleşme anlamları ise yalnızca belirtilen yapılara bağlıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin sayı, miktar ya da ölçü bakımından çok olmayışını bildirir. Bundan yoksulluk ve düşüklük, bir şeyi az sayma veya az gösterme ve belirli yapılarda hiçlik ya da seyrek gerçekleşme anlamları gelişir.

facets.statement: Bir varlığın sayı, miktar veya ölçü bakımından çok olmayışıdır.
Azlık, kişinin yoksullaşması veya toplum içinde düşük ve değersiz görülmesi sonucuna uzanabilir.
Bir şeyi gerçekte ya da değerlendiren kişinin gözünde az sayma ve az gösterme anlamını taşır.
Belirli olumsuzluk ve sıklık yapılarında hiç yokluğu veya bir eylemin pek seyrek gerçekleşmesini anlatır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar azlığın temel sayı ve miktar karşıtlığında birleşir; yoksulluk ve düşüklük, az sayma ve bazı yapılarda yokluğa yaklaşan kullanım bu çekirdeğin düzenli uzantılarıdır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Sayı, miktar veya ölçünün çok olmayışını bildiren temel anlam için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Çokluğun karşıtı olan sayı ve miktar azlığını doğrudan korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir şeyin sayı veya miktar bakımından çok olmadığının söylendiği bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Temel azlık durumunu doğal bir Türkçe yapıyla tam olarak verir.

branches.what_is_ar: القليل والقِلَّة ضد الكثرة، ويدخل فيه الافتقار والذلة، وتقليل الشيء في العين، واستقلاله، واستعمال القليل للنفي أو للندرة
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس علو الشيء ولا الجرة ولا الحمل ولا الرعدة
branches.source_phrase_ar: القل القليل؛ رماه الله بالقل والذل أي بالقلة والذلة (jamhara)؛ شيء قليل وجمعه قلل؛ قل الشيء يقل قلة؛ قلله في عينه؛ أقل افتقر؛ استقله عده قليلا (sihah)؛ قل الشيء يقل قلة فهو قليل وقلال؛ القل من الرجال الخسيس الدنيء؛ قليلة ولا كثيرة؛ قليلا ما يؤمنون؛ قاللت لفلان؛ تقاللت ما أعطاني (tahdhib)؛ القلة والكثرة يستعملان في الأعداد؛ يكنى بالقلة عن الذلة؛ يكنى بها تارة عن العزة؛ قليل يعبر به عن النفي (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir şeyin en üstünü veya başını çekirdek anlam olarak verir; dağın yuvarlak üst bölümü, insan başı ve kılıcın başındaki topuz bu çekirdeğin açık uzmanlaşmalarıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol uzamsal başı ve en üst parçayı bildirir; sayısal azlık ya da büyük kap anlamını içermez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Genel baş ve en üst bölüm anlamı ile dağ tepesi, insan başı ve kılıç topuzu gibi yapıya bağlı uzmanlaşmalar ayrı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin başını veya en üst bölümünü bildirir. Dağın üstteki yuvarlak parçası, insan başı ve kılıcın sap ucundaki topuz bu uzamsal çekirdeğin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Bir nesnenin veya oluşumun başı ya da en üstte bulunan bölümüdür.
Dağın en üstünde yer alan, kimi tanımda yuvarlak biçimli bölümünü adlandırır.
İnsan başı ile kılıcın sap ucundaki başlık veya topuz da aynı üst ve baş kavramıyla adlandırılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar bir şeyin başı ve en üst bölümü üzerinde birleşir; dağ tepesi temel örnektir, insan başı ile kılıç topuzu da aynı biçimsel ve uzamsal çizgide yer alır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi büyük bir küp veya iri kap anlamında birleşir; iki kaplık ölçü ve belirli bir bölgeyle anılan iri küpler de aynı kap anlamını somutlaştırır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol büyük bir kap türünü ve onun ölçü değerini kapsar; nicelik azlığı veya dağ tepesi anlamını kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Büyük küp anlamı çekirdektir; belirli bir bölgeye bağlanan kap adı ile iki kaplık ölçü yalnızca kendi yapılardaki uzmanlaşmalardır.

concept_map.definition: Büyük bir küpü veya küpe benzeyen iri kabı bildirir. Belirli bir bölgenin iri küpleri ve iki böyle kabın aldığı miktar bu kap anlamına bağlı özel kullanımlardır.

facets.statement: Küpe benzeyen, özellikle sıvı taşımaya veya saklamaya elverişli büyük bir kaptır.
Belirli bir bölgeyle anılan iri küpler veya büyük toprak kaplar bu adın tanınmış bir türünü oluşturur.
İki büyük kap, bu iki kabın kendisini veya onların aldığı sıvı miktarını bildiren bir ölçü değeri kazanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar iri bir küp veya büyük kap üzerinde birleşir; tanınmış bölgesel kaplar büyüklüğü örnekler, iki kaplık kullanım ise nesne adını kapasite ölçüsüne taşır.
